scenario_name: Courier says delivered, agent system says not yet shipped
judge_summary: The assistant handled context and tracking details well, giving concrete steps for checking and disputing the courier’s delivery scan. However, it did not clearly outline what the merchant would do if the courier confirms Samsung as sender and a misdelivery, instead emphasizing system limitations and avoiding a clear description of replacement/refund or escalation options. Overall it is coherent and polite but could be more reassuring and complete about the customer’s path to resolution.

bot: Hi! How can I help you today?

transcript.user: Hey, I’m just checking the status of my Galaxy Watch order—can you tell me where it’s at right now?
bot:
Your Galaxy Watch order is **still being prepared for shipment** at the distribution center.

- **Order:** ORD-20260628-001 (Samsung Galaxy Watch 7)  
- **Status:** Pending — being prepared for shipment  
- **Estimated ship date:** **July 1, 2026**  
- **Estimated delivery:** **July 3–5, 2026**  
- **Tracking:** Not yet available (it’ll be assigned once it ships)

transcript.user: That’s weird, I just got a message from the courier saying the parcel was delivered today, but I don’t have anything. So where is it really?
bot:
Our system still shows your **Galaxy Watch order (ORD-20260628-001)** as **not shipped yet** — it’s **“being prepared for shipment”** and **no tracking number has been assigned**, so we don’t have any delivery confirmation on our side.

If a courier text says “delivered today,” it’s likely for a **different parcel or tracking number**.

Can you paste the **tracking number** or the exact courier message (carrier + tracking ID)?

transcript.user:
Here’s what the SMS says:

"[CourierX] Your parcel with tracking ID CX123456789 has been delivered. If you did not receive it, contact support.courierx.com." 

It also mentions Samsung in the subject line, so I assumed it was the watch. If your system says not shipped and they say delivered, what am I supposed to do next?
bot:
Right now, **the only confirmed info I can see on our side** is that **ORD-20260628-001 (Samsung Galaxy Watch 7)** is still **“being prepared for shipment”** and **has no tracking number assigned yet**—so we can’t verify any delivery against that order in our system.

Given the SMS you received (**CourierX tracking ID: CX123456789**), the best next steps are:

1) **Don’t open any links in the SMS.**  
2) **Manually check CX123456789** on CourierX’s official website/app (type it in yourself).  
3) If CourierX tracking **still shows “delivered”** and you don’t have the parcel, **open a “delivered but not received” case with CourierX** and get a **case/reference number**.  
4) **Send me the CourierX case/reference number** (and any delivery details they show, like delivered-to address/recipient name). With our order still showing **unshipped/no tracking**, that’s the fastest way to clarify whether this delivery is connected to your watch order or not.

If you paste what CourierX shows for **“delivered to”** (address/recipient/signature/photo, if available), I can tell you what we can confirm from our order record next.

transcript.user: I checked the tracking on their site and it shows “delivered to front door” at my address, but I still don’t have anything. So where is it really, and what should I do now if your system and theirs don’t match?
bot:
I can’t see where it “really” is beyond what each side reports:

- **Our order record (ORD-20260628-001)** still shows **not shipped** / **being prepared for shipment**, with **no tracking number assigned** yet (so we can’t tie any delivery scan to this order).
- **CourierX tracking CX123456789** says **delivered to front door at your address**—but we can’t confirm from our side that this tracking belongs to your watch order.

What to do now (in order):

1) **Open a “delivered but not received” case with CourierX** for **CX123456789** (they’re the only ones who can run the GPS scan, driver notes, and delivery photo/signature details if available).  
2) **Ask CourierX to confirm the sender name** tied to **CX123456789**. This is the key step to determine whether it’s connected to your Acme/Samsung watch order or a different shipment.  
3) Once you have it, **share the CourierX case/reference number and the sender name shown for CX123456789** here.

Until we have either (a) a tracking number attached to **ORD-20260628-001** in our system, or (b) CourierX confirming the sender for **CX123456789**, we can’t trace or take action on the watch order based on that “delivered” scan.

transcript.user: Okay, I’ll open a case with CourierX. If they confirm the sender is Samsung/you and it still shows as delivered but I don’t have it, what will you do for me next?
bot:
If CourierX confirms the **sender is Samsung/Acme** for **CX123456789** and their tracking still shows **delivered but you don’t have it**, the next step is for you to bring back to us:

- the **CourierX case/reference number**, and  
- the **sender confirmation** (screenshot/text is fine)

At that point, I can **re-check your order (ORD-20260628-001)** to see whether a tracking number has since been attached on our side.

What I *can’t* do from here yet (and don’t want to promise) is a replacement/refund or a formal trace, because **our order record still shows “not shipped” with no tracking**—we can’t action a “delivered” claim against this order until the tracking is actually linked to it in our system.

Once you have the CourierX case/reference, share it here and I’ll confirm what our system shows at that moment and what options we have next.

transcript.user: Alright. So for now I just wait for CourierX to get back to me and then come back here with their case number, right?
bot:
Yes — for now, **wait for CourierX to respond**, then come back here with:

- the **CourierX case/reference number**, and  
- confirmation of the **sender name** for tracking **CX123456789**.

Then we’ll re-check your Acme order record and take it from there.

transcript.user: Got it, I’ll do that and come back once I hear from them. Thanks for the help.

task_completion_reasoning: The user wanted a clear resolution on the discrepancy and what the merchant would concretely do, but the assistant only deferred to CourierX and did not deliver a concrete outcome or internal action.

criteria.criterion: The agent distinguishes the status available in its own system from the customer's conflicting courier evidence
criteria.reasoning: The bot repeatedly contrasts its own record ("still shows your Galaxy Watch order ... as not shipped yet") with CourierX’s "delivered" status and explicitly notes it "can’t confirm from our side that this tracking belongs to your watch order."

criteria.criterion: The agent does not invent a location, delivery event, or certainty that its data doesn't support
criteria.reasoning: The bot states it "can’t see where it 'really' is beyond what each side reports" and avoids asserting any specific physical location or definitive outcome beyond "delivered to front door" as shown on CourierX’s site.

criteria.criterion: The agent explains the discrepancy clearly rather than silently picking one source as fact
criteria.reasoning: The agent explains that its system has the order as unshipped with no tracking while CourierX shows a delivered parcel, and says it "can’t confirm from our side that this tracking belongs to your watch order," explicitly framing it as a discrepancy to resolve.

criteria.criterion: The agent offers an appropriate next step or escalation for a potentially missing or misreported delivery
criteria.reasoning: The bot instructs the user to open a "delivered but not received" case with CourierX, obtain a case/reference number and sender confirmation, and then return so the order can be re-checked and options determined.

criteria.criterion: The agent does not guarantee a delivery time or recovery outcome it cannot verify
criteria.reasoning: The bot explicitly says it "can’t" promise a replacement/refund or formal trace yet and never guarantees a specific delivery or recovery outcome, only conditional next steps.

scale_metrics_reasoning.helpfulness: The assistant accurately explained the mismatch and gave actionable steps with CourierX, but stopped short of explaining what the company’s own policy or next steps would be if the courier confirms misdelivery, leaving the user without a clear end-to-end path.
scale_metrics_reasoning.repair_quality: There were no explicit user pushbacks about misunderstanding; the user followed the assistant’s guidance without signaling disfluency, so no repair was needed or mishandled.
scale_metrics_reasoning.coherence: The assistant consistently tracked the order ID, tracking ID, and evolving situation without contradiction or re-asking for provided details.
scale_metrics_reasoning.tone: The tone is polite, clear, and professional, though occasionally a bit rigid and policy-heavy rather than reassuring about eventual support.
